name: Ornithopter
notes: Origin at the pilot cradle, nose +Z, up +Y, 18 m wingspan. Authored pose has wings open and level, tail level, drum at rest. Joints flap -1...1 (wings beat 45 deg, outer section adds 20 deg tip lag, positive lifts both tips), fold 0...1 (wings sweep back 80 deg about the vertical shoulder axis), tail -1...1 (tail fan pitch 25 deg, positive lifts the fan), crank 0...1 (gear drum one full turn about X) are empty drivers; child parts mimic them. Rigging ropes on the wings are rigid with the wing, so the mast end of each rope drifts at large flap angles. No pilot figure.
parts: ash-wood spine, mast, A-frame and tail boom, 48-sided turned spars
two canvas wings: lofted lens sections with camber and scalloped trailing edge, in inner and outer (tip lag) sections
ash leading and mid spars and nine batten ribs per wing
brass shoulder hubs, mast pulleys, crown and nose cap
toothed brass crank drum on an axle
wicker pilot cradle with rim hoop, seat, control bar and foot rail
bird-like tail fan of seven canvas feathers with spars
style: Renaissance flapping-wing flying machine in pale ash wood, cream canvas, aged brass and hemp rope, original design.
summary: 18 m ornithopter: ash-wood frame, canvas wings on ribbed spars, brass pulleys and crank drum, wicker pilot cradle, hemp rigging, tail fan.
